misconceptions.description: Believing the choice between first and third person in a bio is cosmetic rather than tied to the platform and audience
misconceptions.trigger: learner picks a voice at random or lets a tool decide without considering where the bio will appear
misconceptions.feedback: Match voice to the venue. First person fits a personal LinkedIn About; third person fits a speaker or team-page bio.

misconceptions.description: Opening a bio with stacked adjectives (passionate, results-driven, detail-oriented) that fit almost anyone
misconceptions.trigger: learner's first sentence is a string of personality adjectives with no role or proof
misconceptions.feedback: Open with a role, a focus, and one concrete thing you have done, not a list of interchangeable adjectives.

misconceptions.description: Keeping AI-generated claims of experience or leadership the student does not actually have
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a bio that overstates years of experience or scope of leadership
misconceptions.feedback: A bio must be true. Replace invented seniority with your real level: coursework, a club role, or one project.

misconceptions.description: Writing a bio that states interests and goals but never includes one concrete, checkable accomplishment
misconceptions.trigger: learner's bio lists what they like but names no project, role, or measurable result
misconceptions.feedback: Anchor the bio with one proof: a project, a tool you used, or a number, so the reader has something specific to remember.
